sentences.text:
Member to Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Waraseoni, District Balaghat (for short 'the Tribunal') in Motor Accident Claim Case No.06/2003 had directed Appellant - M.P. Road Transport Corporation to pay 50,000/- along with interest and cost to respondent No.1 - claimant, under its co-extensive liability with respondents No.2 and 3.
2.
The present appeal has been argued on three counts.

First, offending bus was under the control and management of respondent No.3 Chattisgarh Infrastructure Development Corporation and its driver was also in the employment of respondent No.3, therefore, no liability could have been fastened on appellant - M.P. Road Transport Corporation.

Second, the accident occurred on account of negligence of the driver of Trailor and not of the offending bus and third, there was no evidence on the permanent disability caused to respondent No.1 - claimant, therefore, the finding given on this aspect by the Tribunal is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18064 2 MA-625-2005 perverse.
3.
Counsel for appellant has been heard on the merits of the case, while none appeared behalf of respondents.
Record of the Tribunal has been examined.

1 4 .

sentences.text: Appellant has made a contention in this appeal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the driver of Trailor, but the written statement filed before Tribunal by appellant is silent on any such fact.
Moreover, respondent No.1 - claimant was travelling in a passenger bus and was not the driver of any of the vehicles involved in the accident.
Therefore, in this case of composite negligence, he has a legal right to claim compensation from either of the tortfeasors, their owner and the Insurance Company.
Thus, this ground is not sustainable.

5. The impugned award reflects that the Tribunal though reached to a finding of permanent disability caused to respondent No.1 - claimant, but did not assess the compensation on the parameters applicable to a permanent disability case.

Admittedly, respondent No.1 - claimant was aged around 82 years at the time of accident and the Tribunal was of the opinion that on account of injuries sustained in the accident, his old age health issues aggravated and compelled him to face lifelong pain in the injured knee joint.
It can not be ignored that on account of injury in knee joint at this age, his life amenities would have been impaired and life expectancy would have also been whittled.
It appears that having considered this fact, the Tribunal has awarded significant amount towards pain and suffering, which can not be demarked as disproportionate.
Thus, the impugned award is inviolable even on this count.
6. Next comes the question of imposing liability on appellant and respondent No.3 under their joint complicity.

Appellant has claimed that after the division of erstwhile State of Madhya Pradesh in two successor States of Madhya NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18064 3 MA-625-2005 Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, the newly constituted State of Madhya Pradesh vide notification dated 26.07.2001 established the Madhya Pradesh Road transport Corporation with effect from the date of publication of notification.
Said gazette notification is marked as A-3.

The contents of notification provide only for the establishment of Madhya Pradesh Road Transport Corporation with effect from a particular date, but it is silent on the distribution of assets and liabilities of erstwhile State Road Transport Corporation established under the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950.

Annexure-A/2 reveals that for the newly constituted State of Chhattisgarh, the Chhattisgarh Infrastructure Development Corporation was endowed with assets and liabilities in terms of the conditions mentioned in this notification dated 13.12.2002.

Both these notifications do not give any hint on the issue of division of assets and liabilities between the two corporations that came into existence after the Madhya Pradesh Reorganization Act, 2000 was enforced.
7. The answer to aforesaid conundrum does not lie even in Annexure- A/1, which is a gazette published on 26.12.2002 by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways India.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: This notification reveals that no agreement between the successor States of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh was reached for apportionment of assets, rights, and liabilities of erstwhile Madhya Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It, thus, proclaimed that from the appointed date of 31st December, 2002,
the erstwhile Madhya Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation shall cease to function and shall stand dissolved while the rights and liabilities of this Corporation shall be apportioned between the States of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh on the basis of "as is whereas as on 1st November,
2000".

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The principle of "as is where is", as on 1st November 2000, was applied NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18064 4 MA-625-2005 only with respect to division of field staff,
buses, and stores of erstwhile Corporation.
Annexure-A/1 makes no reference to the issue of division M.P.Road Transport Corporation vs Harishanker Agrawal & Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177687164/
2 of liabilities on the basis of same principle of "as is where is" as on 1st November, 2000.

Thus,
Annexure-A/1 the notification dated 27.12.2007, SO No. 1373E gives no strength to the case of appellant for avoiding its liability to pay compensation.
Accordingly, appeal fails on this ground as well.
8. Appeal is accordingly dismissed and disposed of .
Let the compliance of Tribunal given under the impugned award be ensured within 30 days from the passing of this order.

9. Let the copy of this order be sent to the Tribunal along with the record for necessary information and compliance.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE sjk M.P.Road Transport Corporation vs Harishanker Agrawal & Ors.
